Keywords: streaming stream tokens typing generate realtime SSE
Problem: Users stare at a blank screen while a long answer is generated, feels frozen and slow
Solution: Render tokens as they arrive so the user sees progress within ~300ms and can start reading immediately
Do: Stream text incrementally and auto-scroll to keep the newest line visible
Don't: Wait for the full response then dump it all at once
Code Example: for await (const chunk of stream) { el.textContent += chunk.delta }
Anti-Pattern: const res = await fetch(); el.textContent = await res.text() // one big blob
When to Use: Any LLM chat or completion UI where responses exceed one sentence

Keywords: stop cancel abort halt interrupt streaming
Problem: Model goes off on a wrong tangent and the user is forced to wait for it to finish
Solution: Show a Stop button while streaming that aborts the request and keeps the partial text
Do: Swap the Send button for a Stop button during generation and wire it to an AbortController
Don't: Disable all controls until the model finishes
Anti-Pattern: <button disabled>Sending...</button> with no way to cancel
When to Use: Every streaming response, especially long-form or agentic runs

Keywords: thinking reasoning chain-of-thought collapsible steps trace
Problem: Chain-of-thought is either hidden (feels like a black box) or dumped raw (overwhelming)
Solution: Put reasoning in a collapsed 'Thinking' section that users can expand on demand
Do: Collapse reasoning by default with a subtle 'Thought for 4s' summary label
Don't: Force the full reasoning trace inline above every answer
Anti-Pattern:
{fullChainOfThought}
{answer} // always expanded
When to Use: Reasoning models where the thinking trace adds trust but not primary value

Keywords: cursor caret blink typing indicator generating
Problem: Users cannot tell whether the stream is still active or has silently stalled
Solution: Show a blinking cursor or caret at the end of streaming text; remove it when done
Do: Append an animated caret span while streaming and drop it on completion
Don't: Leave text static with no signal that more is coming
Anti-Pattern: no indicator; user cannot distinguish 'done' from 'stalled'
When to Use: Text streaming interfaces to signal liveness

Keywords: markdown rendering code block partial parse format
Problem: Streaming raw markdown shows broken tables and unclosed code fences mid-generation
Solution: Parse and render markdown incrementally, tolerating unclosed blocks until they complete
Do: Use a streaming-tolerant markdown parser and render code blocks once the fence closes
Don't: Re-parse the entire document on every token (janky) or show raw asterisks
Code Example: render(md, { streaming: true }) // tolerates open ``` fences
Anti-Pattern: el.innerHTML = fullMarkdownString // flickers and shows raw syntax
When to Use: Chat UIs rendering markdown or code from a stream

Keywords: composer textarea enter shift-enter newline submit
Problem: Enter submits too early when users want a new line, or newline blocks quick sending
Solution: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a newline; auto-grow the textarea up to a max height
Do: Bind Enter to submit and Shift+Enter to newline, with an auto-resizing textarea
Don't: Make users click a tiny Send button for every message
Anti-Pattern: onKeyDown: if (e.key==='Enter') send() // blocks multiline entirely

Keywords: suggestions starters prompts chips examples empty first-run
Problem: A blank prompt box gives new users no idea what the AI can actually do
Solution: Offer 3-4 tappable example prompts on the empty state to teach capability and lower the barrier
Do: Show contextual example chips that populate the composer when clicked
Don't: Present an empty box with only a generic 'Ask me anything' placeholder
Anti-Pattern: <textarea placeholder='Ask me anything' /> // no guidance
When to Use: First-run / empty state of any AI assistant

Keywords: slash command menu shortcut autocomplete actions
Problem: Power users need fast access to modes and actions without leaving the keyboard
Solution: Trigger a command menu on '/' with fuzzy search over available actions
Do: Open an anchored command palette on '/' and filter as the user types
Don't: Hide all actions behind nested menus that require mouse navigation
Anti-Pattern: buried settings menu; no keyboard command discovery
When to Use: Feature-rich assistants with multiple modes or tools

Keywords: context window tokens limit meter truncation budget
Problem: Users hit the context limit unexpectedly and lose earlier messages silently
Solution: Show a subtle token/context usage meter and warn before truncation happens
Do: Display used/total context and warn at ~90% before older turns are dropped
Don't: Silently drop earlier messages with no warning when the window fills
Anti-Pattern: silently truncate history; user wonders why the AI 'forgot'
When to Use: Long conversations or document-heavy chats near model limits

Keywords: attachment upload image file paste drag drop multimodal
Problem: Users cannot tell whether images/files are supported or that an upload succeeded
Solution: Provide a clear attach affordance plus paste and drag-drop, with per-file preview and remove
Do: Show thumbnail previews with a remove (x) and validate type/size before sending
Don't: Accept a raw file path field with no preview or validation feedback
Anti-Pattern: <input type='file'> with no preview, no error on unsupported type

Keywords: tool call function agent action transparency step
Problem: When the agent calls tools, users see a long pause with no idea what is happening
Solution: Surface each tool call as a labeled step ('Searching the web...', 'Reading file X') in real time
Do: Render each tool invocation as a compact status line with its name and target
Don't: Hide tool activity behind a single ambiguous 'Working...' spinner
Anti-Pattern: <Spinner/> // opaque; user cannot tell what the agent is doing

Keywords: confirmation approval destructive human-in-the-loop guardrail action
Problem: Autonomous agents can send emails, delete data, or spend money without user consent
Solution: Require explicit user approval before any irreversible or outward-facing action, showing exact details
Do: Pause and show a confirmation card with the concrete action, target, and cost before executing
Don't: Let the agent execute side-effectful actions automatically and report after the fact
Code Example: <Confirm action='Send email to client@co' onApprove={run} onDeny={skip}/>
Anti-Pattern: await sendEmail(draft) // fires without asking the user
When to Use: Any agent that can take irreversible or external actions

Keywords: timeline steps plan progress agent multi-step trace
Problem: Multi-step agent runs feel chaotic; users cannot follow what was done or what remains
Solution: Show an ordered, collapsible timeline of planned and completed steps with status icons
Do: Render steps as a vertical timeline with pending/running/done states
Don't: Emit a wall of unstructured log text for a multi-step run
Anti-Pattern: console-style log dump with no structure or status
When to Use: Agents that execute plans of 3+ steps

Keywords: long running task progress background async polling job
Problem: Tasks that take minutes look frozen, so users refresh or abandon them
Solution: Show determinate progress or elapsed time and allow the user to leave and get notified on completion
Do: Report progress/elapsed time and let the task run in the background with a completion notice
Don't: Block the whole UI on a modal spinner for a multi-minute job
Code Example: <Progress value={done} max={total}/> Running 2m 14s — you can leave this open
Anti-Pattern: <ModalSpinner/> blocking UI with no time estimate for 3 minutes
When to Use: Deep research, batch, or heavy generation tasks

Keywords: collapse tool output result verbose json truncate
Problem: Raw tool output (long JSON, full pages) buries the actual answer
Solution: Collapse verbose tool results behind a summary the user can expand if they want detail
Do: Show a one-line result summary with an expandable 'View details' section
Don't: Paste the entire raw tool payload inline into the conversation
Anti-Pattern:
{hugeJsonBlob}
// dominates the transcript
When to Use: Agents whose tools return large payloads

Keywords: citation source attribution reference grounding link footnote
Problem: Users cannot verify AI claims and have no way to check whether an answer is real
Solution: Attach inline citations linking each factual claim to its source document or URL
Do: Add clickable citation markers next to claims that open the exact source
Don't: State facts with total confidence and zero sources
Anti-Pattern: 'The market grew 12%.' // no source, unverifiable
When to Use: RAG, search, and research assistants making factual claims

Keywords: confidence uncertainty hedge probability signal reliability
Problem: AI states guesses with the same confident tone as verified facts, misleading users
Solution: Signal low-confidence or speculative content visually or verbally so users calibrate trust
Do: Distinguish 'I'm not certain, but...' content and let the model hedge honestly
Don't: Force a confident tone on every answer regardless of actual certainty
Anti-Pattern: 'It was definitely 2019.' // false certainty on a guess
When to Use: Any domain where wrong answers carry real cost (health, legal, finance)

Keywords: ai-generated label provenance disclosure watermark badge
Problem: Users or downstream readers mistake AI-generated content for verified human work
Solution: Clearly label AI-generated or AI-assisted output so people can weigh it appropriately
Do: Add an unobtrusive 'AI-generated' badge on generated media and drafts
Don't: Present AI output as indistinguishable from vetted human content
Anti-Pattern: no label; readers assume a human wrote and checked it
When to Use: Generated images, drafts, summaries shown to third parties

Keywords: grounding rag from-your-data source vs general knowledge
Problem: Users cannot tell whether an answer came from their documents or the model's general knowledge
Solution: Visually distinguish grounded answers (from provided context) from ungrounded model knowledge
Do: Tag answers as 'From your documents' vs 'General knowledge' and show which chunks were used
Don't: Blend retrieved facts and model priors with no indication of origin
Anti-Pattern: single answer with no signal whether it used the user's data
When to Use: RAG assistants over private knowledge bases

Keywords: refusal guardrail decline safety blocked policy explain
Problem: Blunt 'I can't help with that' refusals feel arbitrary and frustrate legitimate users
Solution: Explain why a request was declined and offer a safe, constructive alternative when possible
Do: Give a brief honest reason and a redirect toward what you can do
Don't: Return a terse canned refusal with no explanation or path forward
Code Example: I can't help draft that, but I can outline the legal steps to report it safely.
Anti-Pattern: 'I cannot help with that request.' // no reason, no alternative

Keywords: thumbs feedback rating up down quality signal reason
Problem: Product teams get no signal on answer quality and users cannot flag bad output
Solution: Offer lightweight thumbs up/down with an optional reason to capture quality signal
Do: Show subtle 👍/👎 on each response and ask an optional 'what went wrong' on downvote
Don't: Bury feedback in a separate survey nobody opens
Anti-Pattern: no per-message feedback; only a global 'Contact support' link
When to Use: Any AI product that iterates on model or prompt quality

Keywords: regenerate retry rewrite try-again variant redo
Problem: A single mediocre answer leaves users stuck with no easy way to get a better one
Solution: Provide a one-click Regenerate that re-runs the last prompt, optionally with tone/length tweaks
Do: Offer Regenerate plus quick modifiers like 'shorter' or 'more formal'
Don't: Force users to retype the whole prompt to try again
Anti-Pattern: user must copy-paste and resend the prompt manually

Keywords: edit message resubmit fork rewind prompt correction
Problem: A small typo or missing detail in the prompt forces starting the whole thread over
Solution: Let users edit an earlier message and re-run from that point, forking the conversation
Do: Make prior user messages editable and regenerate downstream from the edit
Don't: Lock sent messages so any mistake means a brand-new conversation
Anti-Pattern: sent messages are immutable; only option is a fresh chat

Keywords: compare variants side-by-side ab two answers choose
Problem: Users cannot judge which of several possible answers is best
Solution: Generate two variants side by side and let the user pick the preferred one
Do: Show A/B responses with a 'pick this' control that also feeds preference data
Don't: Overwhelm the user with five variants and no way to choose
Anti-Pattern: auto-pick silently, giving the user no choice or insight

Keywords: memory remember stored profile transparency what-it-knows
Problem: AI silently remembers personal facts, unsettling users who cannot see or control it
Solution: Expose a viewable, editable list of what the assistant has stored about the user
Do: Provide a Memory panel showing each stored fact with edit/delete controls
Don't: Persist user facts invisibly with no way to inspect or remove them
Anti-Pattern: hidden long-term memory the user never sees or consents to

Keywords: memory saved toast notice consent added confirmation
Problem: The AI stores something important without the user realizing it was saved
Solution: Show a brief, dismissible notice when a new memory is written, with undo
Do: Surface a 'Saved to memory' toast with an Undo action when a fact is stored
Don't: Write memories silently with zero acknowledgement
Code Example: toast('Saved to memory: prefers metric units', { action: undo })
Anti-Pattern: silent write; user only discovers it turns later, feels surveilled
When to Use: Products that auto-extract memories from conversation

Keywords: reset clear new chat context fresh forget session
Problem: Prior context leaks into an unrelated new task, producing confusing answers
Solution: Give an obvious 'New chat' / clear-context control and show when context has been reset
Do: Offer a clear New Chat action and visually mark the fresh-context boundary
Don't: Keep one endless thread where old topics contaminate new ones
Code Example: <button onClick={newChat}>+ New chat</button> // starts clean context
Anti-Pattern: single infinite thread; no way to drop stale context

Keywords: latency perceived skeleton optimistic first-token time-to-first
Problem: Even fast models feel slow when nothing happens for the first second
Solution: Optimize time-to-first-token: echo the user message instantly and show an immediate thinking state
Do: Render the user's message and a thinking indicator within ~100ms of send
Don't: Leave the UI static until the full response is ready
Anti-Pattern: await fullResponse(); render() // UI dead for 3s

Keywords: error retry failure recover resume partial network timeout
Problem: A dropped connection mid-stream loses the whole partial response and the user's place
Solution: Preserve partial output on failure and offer Retry that resumes rather than restarts
Do: Keep the partial text, show an inline error, and offer Retry / Continue
Don't: Wipe the partial answer and show a generic full-screen error
Anti-Pattern: catch { clearChat(); alert('Something went wrong') }
When to Use: Any streaming or long-running AI request

Keywords: rate limit quota throttle wait retry-after cooldown busy
Problem: A cryptic 429 or 'error' leaves users unsure whether to retry or give up
Solution: Explain the limit in human terms with a concrete wait time and, if relevant, an upgrade path
Do: Say what happened, when they can retry, and disable send with a countdown
Don't: Show a raw '429 Too Many Requests' or silent failure
Code Example: You've hit the hourly limit. Try again in 4m — upgrade for more.
Anti-Pattern: toast('Error 429') // opaque, actionable to no one

Keywords: cost tokens usage price budget spend meter billing
Problem: Users on metered plans have no idea what a request will cost until the bill arrives
Solution: Show token/cost usage per request or session so users can self-govern spend
Do: Display running cost/usage and warn before an unusually expensive operation
Don't: Hide all usage until an invoice surprises the user
Anti-Pattern: no usage signal anywhere; cost is a black box

Keywords: model selector picker capability speed cost tradeoff choose
Problem: Users pick a model blindly with no sense of its speed, cost, or strengths
Solution: Label each model with plain-language tradeoffs (speed vs depth vs cost), not just a codename
Do: Describe models by what they're good for, with cost/speed hints on the selector
Don't: Offer a dropdown of opaque version strings with no guidance
Code Example: Fast · cheap · everyday   |   Smartest · slower · complex reasoning
Anti-Pattern: <select><option>model-x-2026-v3</option></select> // meaningless to users
When to Use: Products exposing multiple models to end users

Keywords: empty state onboarding first-run capability limits expectations
Problem: New users don't know what the AI can do, its limits, or how to phrase requests
Solution: Use the empty state to set capabilities, limits, and example prompts honestly
Do: Explain what it's good at, note key limits, and offer example prompts
Don't: Drop users into a blank chat with an over-promising 'I can do anything' claim
Anti-Pattern: blank screen implying unlimited, always-correct capability

Keywords: disclaimer limits mistakes can-make-errors honesty footer
Problem: Users over-trust AI output and act on hallucinations without verifying
Solution: Set an honest, non-intrusive reminder that the AI can make mistakes near where output appears
Do: Add a quiet 'AI can make mistakes — verify important info' line at the input
Don't: Imply flawless accuracy or bury the disclaimer where nobody reads it
Code Example: AI can make mistakes. Verify important info.
Anti-Pattern: no caveat anywhere; product implies perfect reliability

Keywords: voice barge-in interrupt talk-over realtime speech stop-speaking
Problem: The AI keeps talking over the user, forcing them to wait through a wrong answer
Solution: Let the user interrupt by speaking; detect voice activity, stop TTS instantly, and start listening
Do: Duck/stop the AI's speech the moment user speech is detected and switch to listening
Don't: Play the full generated audio no matter what the user does
Anti-Pattern: audio.play(); // uninterruptible, user must wait it out
When to Use: Voice assistants and realtime speech agents

Keywords: transcription live captions speech-to-text partial realtime asr
Problem: Users can't tell if the voice agent heard them correctly until it responds wrongly
Solution: Show live partial transcription of the user's speech so they can catch misrecognition early
Do: Stream interim ASR results in gray, finalize in solid text when confidence settles
Don't: Hide the transcript and only reveal what was heard after the AI answers
Anti-Pattern: no transcript; user discovers the mishear only from a wrong reply

Keywords: turn taking listening speaking state voice conversation status
Problem: In voice mode users don't know whether it's their turn to talk or the AI is still thinking
Solution: Show an explicit state: Listening, Thinking, or Speaking, with distinct visual/audio cues
Do: Render a clear mode indicator (waveform when listening, dots when thinking)
Don't: Use one identical animation for every state so users talk over each other
Anti-Pattern: single generic pulsing dot for all states; awkward collisions

Keywords: voice latency filler thinking sound delay acknowledgement backchannel
Problem: Silence after the user stops talking feels like the voice agent crashed
Solution: Acknowledge within ~500ms with a short backchannel ('mm-hmm', a soft tone) while generating
Do: Emit a brief acknowledgement cue immediately, then stream the real reply
Don't: Stay dead silent for 2-3 seconds while the model generates
Anti-Pattern: long silent gap; user repeats themselves thinking it failed
When to Use: Realtime voice where TTFB is noticeable

Keywords: prompt injection untrusted content security instruction override warning
Problem: Malicious text in a webpage or document hijacks the agent to act against the user
Solution: Treat tool/web/document content as untrusted data, never instructions, and flag suspicious directives
Do: Isolate external content, ignore embedded commands, and warn when content tries to instruct the agent
Don't: Feed fetched page text straight into the prompt as if the user wrote it
Code Example: if (looksLikeInjection(webText)) warn('This page tried to give me instructions')
Anti-Pattern: prompt = userMsg + rawWebPage // page can now command the agent
When to Use: Any agent that ingests web pages, emails, or files

Keywords: exfiltration data leak outbound confirm send external destination
Problem: An agent can be tricked into sending private data to an attacker-controlled destination
Solution: Confirm before sending user data to any recipient or URL not chosen by the user
Do: Show the exact data and destination and require approval for outbound sends
Don't: Auto-send data to whatever address the tool or content suggests
Anti-Pattern: await post(urlFromWebpage, userData) // silent exfiltration

Keywords: boundary untrusted quote provenance visual separation tool output
Problem: Users can't distinguish the AI's own words from quoted, possibly-malicious external text
Solution: Visually box and label content that came from tools or the web as external/quoted
Do: Wrap external content in a labeled quote block distinct from the AI's own voice
Don't: Blend fetched text into the AI's reply with no visual boundary
Anti-Pattern: external text rendered identically to the assistant's own answer

Keywords: version history diff compare previous response revision restore
Problem: After regenerating, users lose a previous answer they actually preferred
Solution: Keep prior generations navigable (< 2/3 >) so users can compare and restore any version
Do: Store each regeneration as a version with prev/next navigation and restore
Don't: Overwrite the previous answer irreversibly on every regenerate
Anti-Pattern: regenerate() // old answer gone forever, no way back
When to Use: Generative UIs where users iterate on output

Keywords: flag report eval dataset capture example improve collect
Problem: Bad outputs are noticed but never captured, so the product never improves
Solution: Turn a user's negative feedback into a structured eval example (input, output, expected)
Do: On a downvote, capture the full context into an eval/review queue with the user's note
Don't: Log only a thumbs-down count with no reproducible context
Anti-Pattern: increment(downvotes) // no context, nothing to learn from
When to Use: Teams running a model/prompt improvement loop

Keywords: system prompt custom instructions persona preferences steer persistent
Problem: Users repeat the same preferences ('be concise', 'use British English') every session
Solution: Offer persistent custom instructions applied to every conversation, editable anytime
Do: Provide a settings field for standing preferences and show they're active
Don't: Force users to restate style preferences in every single prompt
Anti-Pattern: no persistence; the AI forgets tone preferences each session
When to Use: Assistants used repeatedly by the same person

Keywords: tone length concise detailed formal casual quick controls modifiers
Problem: Users get a wall of text when they wanted a one-liner, or vice versa
Solution: Give quick, visible controls for length and tone instead of requiring prompt engineering
Do: Offer chips like Concise/Detailed and Formal/Casual that adjust the next response
Don't: Bury tone control inside a paragraph of prompt the user must write
Anti-Pattern: user must write 'please be more concise and formal' every time

Keywords: temperature creativity slider randomness deterministic plain-language
Problem: A raw 'temperature: 0.7' slider is meaningless to non-technical users
Solution: Expose creativity as plain-language options (Precise / Balanced / Creative), not raw numbers
Do: Map sampling settings to human labels with a short description of each
Don't: Show a bare numeric temperature/top-p slider with no explanation
Code Example: [Precise] [Balanced] [Creative] // maps to temperature under the hood
Anti-Pattern: <input type='range' min=0 max=2 /> labeled 'temperature'

Keywords: share link conversation export privacy scrub redact publish
Problem: Sharing an AI chat can leak personal data embedded earlier in the thread
Solution: Let users share a conversation via link, with a privacy review/scrub before it goes public
Do: Preview what will be shared and offer to redact personal info before creating the link
Don't: Generate a public link instantly including all private context
Anti-Pattern: createPublicLink(thread) // no review, leaks earlier PII

Keywords: branch fork tree explore alternative path conversation nonlinear
Problem: Exploring an alternative direction destroys the original conversation path
Solution: Allow branching from any message so users can explore alternatives without losing the main thread
Do: Fork the thread at a chosen message and let users switch between branches
Don't: Force a strictly linear thread where exploring means overwriting
Anti-Pattern: linear-only chat; trying another path erases the current one

Keywords: accessibility aria-live screen reader streaming announce politeness
Problem: Streaming text spams screen readers, re-announcing the whole answer on every token
Solution: Use aria-live='polite' on a stable container and announce completed chunks, not each token
Do: Announce sentence/paragraph boundaries politely; avoid re-reading the full buffer
Don't: Wrap the streaming node in aria-live='assertive' updated per token
Anti-Pattern:
{fullBufferEveryToken}
// unusable
When to Use: Any streaming AI UI aiming for accessibility

Keywords: reduced motion prefers-reduced-motion typing cursor animation a11y
Problem: Blinking cursors and typing animations trigger discomfort for motion-sensitive users
Solution: Respect prefers-reduced-motion: drop the caret blink and typewriter effect, show text plainly
Do: Gate AI-specific animations behind a reduced-motion check
Don't: Force typewriter and pulsing animations on everyone
Anti-Pattern: always-on typing animation ignoring the user's OS setting
When to Use: AI UIs with motion-based streaming affordances

Keywords: rag chunk highlight passage grounding evidence source snippet
Problem: Users see a citation but can't tell which exact sentence in the source backs the claim
Solution: Highlight the specific retrieved passage that grounded the answer when the user opens a source
Do: Deep-link citations to the exact highlighted span in the source document
Don't: Link to the whole 40-page PDF and let the user hunt for the relevant line
Anti-Pattern: [1] // opens page 1, evidence buried on page 30

Keywords: retrieval preview sources found before answer transparency search
Problem: The model answers before the user knows what it actually retrieved to answer from
Solution: Show the retrieved sources (titles/snippets) before or alongside the generated answer
Do: List the top retrieved chunks so users can judge relevance before trusting the synthesis
Don't: Hide retrieval entirely and present only the final synthesized answer
Anti-Pattern: answer appears with no visibility into what was searched or found

Keywords: no answer insufficient not found dont-know abstain grounding honesty
Problem: When the docs lack the answer, the model invents one instead of admitting the gap
Solution: Detect low-relevance retrieval and say 'I couldn't find this in your sources' rather than guess
Do: Abstain honestly when retrieval scores are weak and offer to search wider
Don't: Fabricate a confident answer from unrelated or empty retrieved context
Code Example: if (topScore < threshold) return 'Not found in your documents.'
Anti-Pattern: generate a plausible answer despite zero relevant retrieval
When to Use: Closed-domain RAG where wrong answers are costly

Keywords: freshness recency as-of date stale cutoff data timestamp
Problem: Users act on data without knowing how old it is or when it was last indexed
Solution: Stamp answers and sources with an 'as of' date so users can judge staleness
Do: Show the source/index date near retrieved facts and flag clearly stale data
Don't: Present time-sensitive facts with no indication of when they were true
Anti-Pattern: 'The price is $40.' // from a doc indexed 8 months ago, unlabeled
When to Use: RAG over changing data (prices, docs, policies)

Keywords: synthesis multiple sources merge conflict attribution combine
Problem: An answer blends several sources, so users can't tell which fact came from where
Solution: Attribute each synthesized claim to its specific source and surface source conflicts
Do: Map each sentence to its source and flag when sources disagree
Don't: Merge multiple documents into one confident voice with a single generic citation
Code Example: The A2 model ships Q3<cite>[2]</cite> at $30<cite>[5]</cite>.
Anti-Pattern: single [1] footnote for an answer synthesized from five documents

Keywords: handoff multi-agent routing which agent active transfer orchestration
Problem: In a multi-agent system users have no idea which specialist is currently handling them
Solution: Name and surface the active agent on handoff so the transition is legible, not jarring
Do: Announce handoffs ('Routing you to the billing specialist') and label the active agent
Don't: Silently swap agents mid-conversation with no signal or context carry-over
Code Example: <Banner>Handed off to Billing Agent</Banner> // context preserved
Anti-Pattern: tone and knowledge shift abruptly with no explanation of who's talking

Keywords: delegation subagent tree orchestrator spawned parallel fan-out
Problem: An orchestrator spawns sub-agents and the user sees only a long unexplained pause
Solution: Visualize the delegation tree: which sub-agents were spawned, their task, and status
Do: Show sub-agents as a nested/indented live tree with per-node status
Don't: Collapse all parallel sub-agent work into one opaque 'Working...' state
Anti-Pattern: no visibility into fan-out; a 3-minute silence with no structure

Keywords: consensus disagreement multiple agents vote compare verify agree
Problem: Multiple agents reach different conclusions and the UI hides the disagreement
Solution: Surface when agents disagree and show the divergence rather than papering over it
Do: Display each agent's verdict and highlight agreement vs conflict for the user to judge
Don't: Average or silently pick one agent's answer, hiding that others disagreed
Code Example: <Verdicts items={agents} /> // 2 agree, 1 dissents — shown to user
Anti-Pattern: return agents[0].answer // dissent discarded invisibly

Keywords: orchestrator plan progress phase step multi-agent overview control
Problem: Long multi-agent runs feel unbounded; users can't tell how far along or intervene
Solution: Show an orchestrator-level plan with phases, current step, and a way to pause or steer
Do: Render the overall plan with a progress marker and a stop/redirect control
Don't: Run the whole plan to completion with no progress signal or off-ramp
Anti-Pattern: opaque long-running job with no plan view and no way to intervene

Keywords: diff edit rewrite change track suggestion inline redline
Problem: When AI rewrites text, users can't see what changed versus their original
Solution: Show AI edits as an inline diff (additions/deletions) rather than a wholesale replacement
Do: Render rewrites as tracked changes the user can scan before accepting
Don't: Replace the user's text with a new block, hiding what was actually changed
Code Example: <Diff before={original} after={rewrite} /> // green add, red strike
Anti-Pattern: setText(aiRewrite) // original overwritten, changes invisible

Keywords: accept reject per-change granular apply suggestion hunk approve
Problem: Users are forced to accept or reject an entire AI rewrite all-or-nothing
Solution: Let users accept or reject each individual change, not the whole suggestion at once
Do: Offer per-hunk Accept/Reject so users keep the good edits and drop the bad ones
Don't: Provide a single Apply-all button for a rewrite touching many spots
Anti-Pattern: <button>Apply all changes</button> // one bad edit taints the lot

Keywords: draft final review status generated confidence editable provisional
Problem: AI-generated content looks final, so users ship it without reviewing
Solution: Mark generated content as a Draft that visibly requires review before it's treated as final
Do: Badge output as 'Draft — review before sending' until the user confirms
Don't: Present generated drafts styled identically to approved, sent content
Anti-Pattern: generated email looks sent-ready; user fires it without a read
When to Use: Drafting tools that produce outbound content

Keywords: template variable placeholder fill merge fields review generated
Problem: AI fills a template but silently leaves or guesses unfilled placeholders
Solution: Highlight AI-filled variables and flag any it couldn't confidently complete
Do: Visually mark filled fields and force review of low-confidence or empty ones
Don't: Silently insert a plausible guess for missing merge fields
Anti-Pattern: 'Dear John' inserted as a guess when the name was actually unknown

Keywords: length limit word count target constraint verbose trim respect
Problem: User asks for a tweet-length reply and gets four paragraphs
Solution: Respect explicit length constraints and show a live count against the target
Do: Honor requested limits and surface a counter (e.g. 240/280) while generating
Don't: Ignore the stated limit and over-generate, forcing the user to trim
Anti-Pattern: produce 600 words when the user asked for 'one sentence'

Keywords: adaptive personalized history suggestion learn recent context
Problem: Starter prompts stay generic and ignore what the user actually does repeatedly
Solution: Adapt suggestions to the user's recent tasks and patterns, not a static list
Do: Surface suggestions derived from recent history, clearly marked as personalized
Don't: Show the same fixed example prompts to a first-timer and a daily power user
Anti-Pattern: identical hardcoded starters regardless of usage
When to Use: Repeat-use assistants with a history signal

Keywords: learn preference opt-in explicit consent adapt personalize control
Problem: The AI adapts to inferred preferences the user never agreed to or can see
Solution: Make preference learning explicit and opt-in, with visible, revertible learned traits
Do: Ask before learning long-term preferences and show what was inferred
Don't: Silently build a behavioral profile and act on it without disclosure
Code Example: toast('Noticed you prefer bullet points — apply always?', {yes,no})
Anti-Pattern: auto-adapts tone/format from tracking with no consent or visibility

Keywords: reset personalization clear profile fresh neutral default control
Problem: Personalization drifts wrong and users have no way to start clean
Solution: Provide a one-click reset that clears learned preferences and returns to neutral defaults
Do: Offer 'Reset personalization' separate from clearing chat history
Don't: Bake personalization in permanently with no escape hatch
Anti-Pattern: no reset; a bad inference biases every future answer forever

Keywords: training data consent opt-out privacy usage improve model toggle
Problem: Users don't know their conversations may train the model, eroding trust when discovered
Solution: Disclose data usage plainly and offer a clear, honored opt-out from training
Do: State whether chats are used for training and provide an easy, respected toggle
Don't: Bury training usage in a ToS and default everyone in silently
Code Example: <Toggle label='Use my chats to improve the model' default={false} />
Anti-Pattern: chats train the model by default; opt-out hidden 6 clicks deep
When to Use: Any product that may train on user data

Keywords: permission scope access agent tools connect grant least-privilege
Problem: An agent requests broad access ('read all your email') with no granularity
Solution: Request least-privilege, scoped permissions and show exactly what the agent can touch
Do: Ask for the narrowest scope needed and list granted capabilities transparently
Don't: Demand blanket account access up front for a narrow task
Anti-Pattern: 'Grant full access to your account' for a one-off calendar lookup
When to Use: Agents that connect to user accounts/tools

Keywords: onboarding guided first task activation walkthrough success first-run
Problem: New users bounce because they never complete one successful action with the AI
Solution: Guide the user through one real, successful task on first run to prove the value fast
Do: Offer a concrete guided first task with a visible success moment
Don't: Drop users at a blank prompt and hope they figure out a good use themselves
Code Example: <GuidedTask steps={firstWin} /> // ends in a real, shareable result
Anti-Pattern: empty chat, no path to a first success; user leaves unconvinced
When to Use: First-run activation of any AI product

Keywords: notification done complete background async finished alert return
Problem: Users start a long task, switch away, and never learn it finished
Solution: Notify on completion of long/background tasks so users can safely leave and return
Do: Send an in-app or push notice when a background run completes, with a deep link
Don't: Require users to sit and watch a multi-minute task to catch the result
Code Example: notify('Your research report is ready', { link: result })
Anti-Pattern: no completion signal; user must keep the tab open and staring

Keywords: proactive suggestion initiate ambient assistant nudge unprompted opt-in
Problem: An assistant that only ever reacts misses chances to help at the right moment
Solution: Let the AI proactively suggest help at relevant moments, always dismissible and non-blocking
Do: Offer timely, dismissible suggestions the user can ignore without friction
Don't: Interrupt with modal, unprompted AI suggestions that block the task
Code Example: <Nudge dismissible>Want me to summarize this thread?</Nudge>
Anti-Pattern: <Modal>AI suggestion!</Modal> // blocks work, can't be ignored

Keywords: digest summary recap periodic batch briefing catch-up notification
Problem: Users drown in raw activity and want the AI to distill it, not add more noise
Solution: Offer an on-demand or scheduled digest that summarizes what changed since last visit
Do: Provide a concise, skimmable recap with links to detail, on the user's cadence
Don't: Push every individual event as its own AI notification
Anti-Pattern: 50 separate 'AI noticed X' pings instead of one digest

Keywords: trace debug inspect prompt response tokens developer observability replay
Problem: When output is wrong, developers can't see the exact prompt, context, and params used
Solution: Expose a per-response trace: full prompt, retrieved context, tool calls, tokens, and settings
Do: Give a developer-facing 'Inspect' that reveals the complete request/response trace
Don't: Show only the final answer, leaving debugging to guesswork
Anti-Pattern: no trace; a bad answer is unreproducible and un-debuggable
When to Use: Developer tools and internal AI dashboards

Keywords: regression alert eval quality drop monitor score baseline degrade
Problem: A prompt or model change silently degrades quality and nobody notices for weeks
Solution: Track eval scores over time and alert when a change regresses a key metric
Do: Chart quality metrics against a baseline and flag statistically real drops
Don't: Ship prompt/model changes with no before/after quality measurement
Code Example: if (score < baseline - delta) alert('Quality regression on eval set')
Anti-Pattern: deploy a new prompt on vibes; regressions discovered via complaints
When to Use: Teams iterating on prompts/models in production

Keywords: follow-up suggested questions next continue explore drill-down chips
Problem: After an answer, users don't know what else they can usefully ask
Solution: Offer 2-3 relevant follow-up questions to help users go deeper without prompt-writing
Do: Surface contextual follow-up chips derived from the current answer
Don't: End the answer with a dead-end and no path to continue
Code Example: <FollowUps items={['How does that compare to X?', ...]} />
Anti-Pattern: no suggested next steps; conversation stalls after one answer

Keywords: query reformulation did-you-mean refine rephrase clarify ambiguous
Problem: A vague or ambiguous query yields a bad answer with no path to fix the input
Solution: Detect ambiguity and offer to refine the query or ask one clarifying question first
Do: Propose a sharper rephrasing or ask a single targeted clarifying question
Don't: Answer an ambiguous query confidently in the wrong interpretation
Code Example: 'Did you mean sales in 2025 or all-time?' before answering
Anti-Pattern: silently assume one meaning and answer the wrong question

Keywords: answer explore split direct sources drill detail progressive
Problem: Users get either a terse answer with no depth or a wall of detail with no takeaway
Solution: Lead with a direct answer, then offer an expandable 'explore' layer for depth and sources
Do: Give the headline answer first, with progressive disclosure for the reasoning and sources
Don't: Force users to read the full analysis to extract a one-line answer
Anti-Pattern: bury the actual answer under five paragraphs of preamble

Keywords: mobile composer thumb reach bottom input one-hand ergonomics
Problem: The prompt input and send sit out of thumb reach on tall phones
Solution: Anchor the composer and primary actions in the bottom thumb zone for one-handed use
Do: Keep the input, send, and voice controls within the bottom third of the screen
Don't: Place the send button at the top of the screen where thumbs can't reach
Code Example: position: sticky; bottom: 0 with actions in the reachable band
Anti-Pattern: send button top-right; requires a two-handed reach every message

Keywords: mobile voice toggle push-to-talk hands-free switch input mode
Problem: Typing long prompts on mobile is painful and there's no fast voice path
Solution: Offer a prominent, one-tap voice input mode alongside typing on mobile
Do: Provide an easy push-to-talk / voice toggle in the composer
Don't: Hide voice input behind a menu, defaulting to slow on-screen typing
Code Example: <button aria-label='Voice input'>🎤</button> // in the composer bar
Anti-Pattern: voice buried in settings; long prompts require thumb-typing
When to Use: Mobile assistants where input length is high

Keywords: mobile streaming scroll interrupt read pace stop autoscroll control
Problem: Aggressive auto-scroll on mobile yanks the view while the user is reading earlier text
Solution: Pause auto-scroll when the user scrolls up; show a 'jump to latest' affordance instead
Do: Detect manual scroll-up and stop forcing the view to the newest token
Don't: Force-scroll to the bottom on every token regardless of where the user is reading
Anti-Pattern: every token snaps the viewport down; re-reading is impossible

Keywords: cutoff knowledge date training recent events limitation disclose
Problem: Users ask about recent events and get confidently outdated answers
Solution: Disclose the model's knowledge cutoff and flag when a query likely needs fresher data
Do: State the cutoff when relevant and offer to search live for recent topics
Don't: Answer time-sensitive questions as if the model's knowledge were current
Code Example: 'My training goes to early 2026 — want me to search for newer info?'
Anti-Pattern: confidently answer 'who won last week' from stale training data

Keywords: fact opinion label distinguish subjective claim judgment hedge
Problem: The AI states subjective judgments in the same authoritative tone as verifiable facts
Solution: Distinguish verifiable facts from the model's opinions or interpretations
Do: Frame subjective content as opinion ('In my assessment...') vs stated fact
Don't: Present interpretations and recommendations as objective, settled truth
Code Example: 'Fact: revenue rose 12%. My read: the trend is fragile.'
Anti-Pattern: 'The strategy is wrong.' // opinion delivered as fact

Keywords: escalate human handoff support agent transfer limit fallback
Problem: The AI loops uselessly on a request it can't handle instead of getting a human
Solution: Detect when the AI is stuck or the stakes are high and offer a clean human handoff
Do: Provide an obvious 'talk to a human' path and pass full context on escalation
Don't: Trap the user in an AI loop with no route to a person
Code Example: <button onClick={escalate}>Talk to a human</button> // sends transcript
Anti-Pattern: endless AI retries; no escape to human support

Keywords: sensitive crisis safety mental-health harm care resources tone
Problem: The AI responds to distress or crisis with a generic, tone-deaf, or unsafe reply
Solution: Detect sensitive contexts and respond with care, appropriate resources, and no false expertise
Do: Shift to a careful tone, avoid clinical overreach, and surface real help resources
Don't: Handle a crisis message like any other query with a breezy generic answer
Anti-Pattern: reply to a distress message with an upbeat generic productivity tip
When to Use: Any consumer assistant reachable by vulnerable users

Keywords: fallback model failover degrade backup switch retry alternative resilience
Problem: When the primary model is down or overloaded, the whole feature just fails
Solution: Fall back to an alternate model on failure and quietly note the degraded mode
Do: Retry on a backup model automatically and, if quality differs, tell the user
Don't: Return a hard error the moment the primary model is unavailable
Code Example: catch { return callFallbackModel(prompt) } // note reduced capability
Anti-Pattern: 500 error to the user whenever the primary provider hiccups

Keywords: content filter blocked safety flagged explain moderation transparency
Problem: A moderation filter blocks output with a blank or cryptic message
Solution: When a safety filter triggers, explain briefly what happened and what the user can do
Do: Give a short, non-accusatory reason and a path to rephrase or appeal
Don't: Return an empty response or a bare 'content blocked' with no context
Code Example: 'That response was filtered for safety. Try rephrasing your request.'
Anti-Pattern: silent empty output; user thinks the app is broken

Keywords: budget cap spend limit cost control ceiling guard alert quota
Problem: Automated agents can rack up large API costs with no ceiling
Solution: Let users set a spend cap and warn or pause when a run approaches the limit
Do: Expose a budget ceiling and halt or confirm before exceeding it
Don't: Run agents unbounded with no cost ceiling or warning
Code Example: if (runCost > cap) pause('Budget cap reached — continue?')
Anti-Pattern: agent loops burn $50 of tokens with no cap or alert

Keywords: batch realtime async cost tradeoff cheaper wait speed choice
Problem: Users pay realtime prices for work that isn't urgent
Solution: Offer a cheaper batch/async option for non-urgent tasks alongside realtime
Do: Let users trade speed for cost with a clear batch option and ETA
Don't: Force every request through the expensive realtime path
Anti-Pattern: no async tier; overnight bulk jobs billed at realtime rates

Keywords: skeleton placeholder structure loading progressive shape scaffold
Problem: A blank area during generation gives no sense of the answer's shape or length
Solution: Show a structural skeleton (headings, list rows) that fills in as content streams
Do: Render placeholder structure matching the expected output, then hydrate it
Don't: Show a bare spinner with no hint of the response's structure or size
Code Example: <Skeleton lines={3} /> then swap in streamed content
Anti-Pattern: <Spinner/> // no structural preview, feels longer than it is

Keywords: prefetch predictive speculative start early intent warm anticipate
Problem: Generation only starts after the user hits send, adding avoidable wait
Solution: Warm up or speculatively start on strong intent signals (pause, selection) to cut latency
Do: Prefetch likely context or pre-warm the model on clear intent, discard if unused
Don't: Do all setup lazily after send, so the user waits through cold-start every time
Anti-Pattern: everything begins at send; no speculative warm-up

Keywords: limits cant-do boundaries capability honest scope expectations
Problem: Users assume the AI can do things it can't, then feel misled when it fails
Solution: State key limits up front ('I can't access the internet / your files') alongside strengths
Do: Show an honest 'what I can and can't do' card during onboarding
Don't: Market unbounded capability and let users discover limits through failure
Anti-Pattern: 'Ask me anything!' with no mention of real constraints
When to Use: First-run of any assistant with hard limits

Keywords: sample example preview output quality show expectation demo before
Problem: Users can't tell what 'good' output looks like before investing effort in a prompt
Solution: Show a real sample input and its output so users calibrate expectations instantly
Do: Preview a concrete example result, not just a description of the feature
Don't: Describe the feature in abstract copy with no example of the actual output
Anti-Pattern: 'Generates professional summaries' // no sample to judge quality

Keywords: keyboard accessibility navigation focus shortcuts operate a11y no-mouse
Problem: Core chat actions (send, stop, regenerate, copy) require a mouse
Solution: Make every primary AI action keyboard-operable with visible focus and shortcuts
Do: Provide focusable controls, logical tab order, and documented shortcuts
Don't: Bind actions to click-only handlers with no keyboard equivalent
Code Example: onKeyDown handlers for send/stop/regenerate + visible :focus-visible ring
Anti-Pattern: regenerate/stop only reachable by mouse; no focus indication
When to Use: Any AI interface aiming for accessibility

Keywords: alt text generated image accessibility describe screen reader caption
Problem: AI-generated images ship with no alt text, invisible to screen-reader users
Solution: Auto-generate descriptive alt text for AI images and let users edit it before use
Do: Produce and attach editable alt text to every generated image
Don't: Output images with empty or filename-only alt attributes
Anti-Pattern: // inaccessible generated media

Keywords: continuity resume session pick-up-where recap return context bridge
Problem: Returning users are dropped cold with no bridge to what they were doing last time
Solution: On return, offer a short recap and a one-tap resume of the prior task or thread
Do: Surface 'Pick up where you left off' with a concise recap of recent context
Don't: Start every session from zero, forcing users to rebuild context manually
Anti-Pattern: cold blank start; user re-explains context they gave yesterday

Keywords: citation streaming anchor stable reflow inline attach live source
Problem: Citations added after streaming cause text to reflow and jump under the reader
Solution: Reserve space and anchor citation markers during streaming to avoid layout jumps
Do: Attach citation markers inline as they stream, with stable reserved positioning
Don't: Append all citations after streaming, shifting text the user is mid-read on
Code Example: inline <cite> tokens streamed in place; no post-hoc reflow
Anti-Pattern: citations injected at end → paragraph reflows, reader loses place
When to Use: Streaming RAG answers with inline sources

Keywords: history recall previous prompt up-arrow reuse edit resend composer
Problem: Users retype or hunt for a prompt they sent minutes ago
Solution: Let users recall and edit recent prompts quickly (e.g. Up-arrow in an empty composer)
Do: Provide keyboard recall of prior prompts for fast reuse and iteration
Don't: Force users to scroll the transcript and copy-paste an old prompt
Anti-Pattern: no recall; iterating on a prompt means retyping it each time

Keywords: undo revert AI action mistake reverse rollback safety confidence
Problem: When an AI applies a change or action, a mistake feels irreversible and scary
Solution: Provide immediate undo for AI-applied actions so users act with confidence
Do: Offer a prominent Undo right after any AI-applied change, with a grace window
Don't: Apply AI actions with no undo, making every acceptance high-stakes
Code Example: toast('Applied AI edit', { action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: revert } })
Anti-Pattern: AI action committed instantly, no undo; users hesitate to try it
When to Use: AI tools that mutate user content or state

Keywords: empty no results zero guidance next-step suggestion recover dead-end
Problem: When the AI finds nothing, users hit a dead-end with no idea what to try next
Solution: Turn empty results into guidance: why nothing matched and concrete next steps
Do: Explain the likely reason for no result and suggest a broader or altered query
Don't: Show a bare 'No results' with no explanation or recovery path
Code Example: 'Nothing matched "X". Try removing filters or searching "Y".'
Anti-Pattern: 'No results found.' // dead-end, no way forward
